intuition.title: Nucleation induction and precursor clusters
intuition.summary: The 0.45-equivalent induction period is interpreted as buildup toward supersaturation before ZnO nucleation, following the LaMer model (reference 39). Basic zinc acetate clusters are proposed as the precursors (references 35 and 40).

intuition.title: Surface cleaning and concurrent ripening
intuition.summary: Dodecylamine is proposed to ligate and solvate surface-exposed dopants. Sharper EPR supports a more homogeneous internal Mn environment. Heating also causes further Ostwald ripening, so cleaning and size evolution are coupled.

general_background.title: Amine coordination
general_background.summary: An amine nitrogen can donate electron density to suitable solution species or surface sites. Donation from the nitrogen lone pair and competition with other ligands can change precursor speciation and surface association.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

general_background.title: Destabilizing a particle dispersion
general_background.summary: An antisolvent can solvate a particle's ligand shell less favourably than the original dispersion medium. Reduced solvation can weaken colloidal stability and allow particles to aggregate and separate from the liquid, depending on the ligands and solvent mixture.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

general_background.title: Solvent and transport
general_background.summary: A solvent carries dissolved species and transports heat through a reaction or dispersion. Solubility, viscosity and molecular interactions affect how precursors and ligand-coated particles move and mix.
